This second application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.287/2022, registered at Police Station Bichhiwara, District Dungarpur, for offences under Sections 363, 366, 344, 376(2), 376(3) IPC and Section 5/6 of the POCSO Act.
The first bail application of the petitioner was dismissed by this Court vide order 12.07.2023.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

Drawing attention of the Court towards the statements of the prosecutrix before competent criminal court, learned counsel for [2023:RJ-JD:44004] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-13459/2023] the petitioner submitted that the prosecutrix in her court statements has admitted the fact of travelling with the petitioner to various places by using public transportation and staying with him for two months and working as a labourer.

Learned counsel submitted that it is highly improbable that the prosecutrix who had remained in company of the present petitioner for more than two months did not disclose Ashok vs The State Of Rajasthan ... on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74507994/

sentences.text: the factum of she being abducted or subjected to sexual assault by the present petitioner to anyone despite having ample opportunities to do so.

Lastly, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that statements of the prosecutrix have already been recorded before competent criminal court and therefore, now there is no apprehension of she being influenced by the present petitioner.

The petitioner who is aged about 19 years is in judicial custody since 30.11.2022 and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time to conclude, therefore, the benefit of bail should be granted to the accused-petitioner.
Learned Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the bail application.

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this court prima facie finds that the prosecutrix in her court statements recorded before the competent criminal court stated that she had remained in the company of petitioner for more than two months and had travelled to various places with him by using public transportation.

In the prima facie opinion of this Court, the argument of learned counsel for the petitioner that the prosecutrix and the petitioner were in a consensual relationship and she voluntarily eloped with him and [2023:RJ-JD:44004] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-13459/2023] remained in his company out of her free will and volition, cannot be brushed aside.
Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/ demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
Consequently, the second bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner Ashok S/o Kanti Lal arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.287/2022, registered at Police Station Bichhiwara, District Dungarpur, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/-
each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 7-Prashant/-
